newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Tyco volume jumps on buyout bid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Tyco volume jumps on buyout bid.

text.p: Trading in individual equity options Monday was highlighted by a sharp increase in activity in Tyco Toys Inc options as the stock rallied on a buyout offer from Mattel Inc.
The stock transaction values Tyco shares at about $12-1/2 each. The toymaker ended up 4-1/2 at 11-1/2 on heavy consolidated volume of 8.1 million shares.
Between puts and calls, about 2,000 Tyco options traded, 10 to 15 times their normal volume. Most turnover was on the call side.
The most active was the December 7-1/2 call, which traded about 615 contracts. The option, with open interest of 720 through last Friday, rose 3-1/2 to four.
Other busy calls included the December 5, the January 10 and the March 10. The most active put was the March 10, which traded 80 contracts.
Ron Ianieri at Gateway Partners in Philadelphia said several strategies were being taken, including buy-writes and outright call and put buying.
"Some people were trying to buy calls in case there's a higher bid," he said.
"Others are going ahead and buying puts to protect the fact that the stock can fluctuate a lot between the time the deal is consummated with a handshake and the time stock is received."
Mattel options were slightly more active than usual, with trading highlighted by spreads in the January 30 puts and calls, each of which traded about 2,000 contracts.
The January 30 call ended down 1/4 at 1-7/16 and the corresponding put rose 3/16 to 1-1/4.
Mattel shares slipped 3/4 to 29-7/8.
In other trading, a large spread was seen in Hilton Hotels Corp options on the Pacific Stock Exchange.
Nearly 5,800 of the Hilton December 27-1/2 calls traded and about 5,525 of the Hilton December 30 calls traded.
Most of the volume was crossed as spreads, the largest block of which was around 4,480 contracts.
Hilton shares ended 5/8 lower at 28-1/4 on turnover of about 1.44 million shares.
Heavy trading was seen in the BankAmerica Corp January 90 calls, which traded 4,915 contracts, ending up 1/4 at eight.
Most of the volume was small lots of around 100, but one block of 1,250 contracts crossed in afternoon trading.
BankAmerica shares rose 1-3/8 to 96.
